purpose: 영어 초록 문장에 대한 확신/완화(certainty/hedging) 단서 사전. Notion 계획 ⑥ '영어 원문 교차 확인'용. 문장별로 Sumner et al. 2014 (BMJ; web appendix ww1 코딩표로 검증) 7단계 인과 주장 강도(0-6)를 부여하고, 이를 한국어 사전과 같은 단정/가능성/연관/무관 4범주로 접어서(collapsed_ko) 번역문의 한국어 사전 라벨과 일치율을 계산한다. 규칙 평가는 대소문자 무시(re.IGNORECASE)로 수행하되 효과 측정치 약어(OR/HR/RR/IRR/CI)는 (?-i:...) 그룹으로 대소문자를 구분한다(provenance_policy.matching 참조).

status_values.verified_source_text: 원문(본문·부록)에서 그 단서 문구(또는 그 직접 굴절형)와 단계를 직접 확인한 항목. 항목마다 source_quote 에 원문 인용을 둔다. status 는 '문구→단계' 대응에 대한 것이고, 정규식 형태(굴절형 확장, lookaround 제외 규칙, 목적어 명사 목록 등)는 pattern_status='project_operationalisation' 으로 따로 표시한다.
status_values.project_extension_of_verified_category: 원문에 그 문구는 없지만 원문이 정의한 범주(예: Sumner level 6 'Direct causal statement')의 동의어·파생형으로 이 프로젝트가 추가한 항목. extends_category 와 extends_quote 에 확장한 범주를 적는다. 휴리스틱으로 보고한다.
status_values.project_addition: 검증된 범주의 확장으로도 정당화하기 어려운 프로젝트 추가 항목. 휴리스틱으로 보고하고 사람 검증으로 확인한다.
status_values.unverified_from_memory: 인용 출처에 있다고 기억하지만 원문과 대조하지 못한 항목(Hyland 2005 목록 전체, Adams 2017 자극 문구, BioScope 홈페이지 키워드 목록).
status_values.verified_lecture_pdf: 첨부된 수업 PDF(W5_1_Text_Preprocessing_2.pdf)에서 본문 그대로 확인한 항목. 페이지 번호는 pdftotext 기준.

provenance_policy.network_note: v3(2026-10-30): Europe PMC 접근이 열려 Sumner 2014 본문(PMC4262123)과 web appendix ww1, Vincze 2008 본문(PMC2586758)을 원문 대조했고 Sumner 2014 / Adams 2017 / Vincze 2008 의 서지 메타데이터를 확인했다(citation_status). Adams 2017 본문과 Hyland 2005(단행본)는 여전히 접근 불가.
provenance_policy.matching: pattern은 Python re 모듈용 정규식이며 최상위 대안(alternative)은 모두 \b 단어 경계, lookbehind, 또는 (?-i: 로 시작해야 한다(compile_lexicon 이 검사해 경고; allow_unanchored=true 인 항목만 예외). re.IGNORECASE 로 컴파일하되, 대문자여야만 뜻이 있는 효과 측정치 약어 OR/HR/aHR/RR/aRR/IRR/CI 는 (?-i:...) 인라인 그룹으로 대소문자를 구분한다('2 or 3 doses', '24 hr' 오탐 방지). 매칭은 토큰화 전 원문 문장의 NFKC 뷰(W5 p.29)에 대해 수행하고 casefold 는 하지 않는다(대소문자 구분 그룹 때문). 축약형은 W5 p.32 Option 1(보존)대로 그대로 두고 n't 는 negation modifier 의 n't\b 대안으로 직접 매칭한다. type 이 evidence_flag_types 에 속하는 항목은 문장 level 을 정하지 않고 evidence_flags 로만 기록된다.
provenance_policy.pattern_status_note: 모든 pattern 은 원문 문구를 정규식으로 옮긴 프로젝트 조작화(operationalisation)다. 단순 굴절형 이상의 제한(lookbehind/lookahead, 목적어 명사 목록, 사이에 끼는 단어 허용 등)이 있는 항목은 pattern_status='project_operationalisation' 과 pattern_note 로 표시한다.

sources.citation: Sumner P, Vivian-Griffiths S, Boivin J, Williams A, Venetis CA, Davies A, Ogden J, Whelan L, Hughes B, Dalton B, Boy F, Chambers CD. The association between exaggeration in health related science news and academic press releases: retrospective observational study. BMJ 2014;349:g7015. doi:10.1136/bmj.g7015
sources.what_used: Methods: unit of coding (main statements; for journal articles the abstract and discussion), the seven point scale with one example sentence per level, and the 'stronger statements trumped weaker ones' rule.
verified_quotes: For journal articles we used the abstract and discussion. We used a seven point scale to rate increasing levels of determinism, where the presence of stronger statements trumped weaker ones

correlational (for example, “drinking wine is associated with increased cancer rates”), ambiguous (for example, “drinking wine linked to cancer risk”), conditional causal (for example, “drinking wine might increase cancer risk”), can cause (for example, “drinking wine can increase cancer risk”), and unconditionally causal (for example, “drinking wine increases cancer risk”)
sources.verify_against: done: full text PMC4262123 (Europe PMC) Methods section, read 2026-10-30.

sources.citation: Sumner P et al. BMJ 2014;349:g7015, web appendix ww1 (supplementary methods incl. the table of examples for the relationship-statement levels), downloaded from Europe PMC supplementaryFiles for PMC4262123.
sources.what_used: the original coding manual: definition and example phrases for levels 0-6, the strongest-statement rule, and the separate 'explicitly probabilistic' binary code with its example words.
verified_quotes: the IV (or pseudo IV in correlational designs), DV and stated relationship between them (if any) were extracted from the main claims, which were operationalized as the title plus first two sentences in PRs and news. For the JA, main claims were defined within the abstract and discussion sections.

0. No relationship stated (but could have been): The study must have contained at least two variables (IV and DV, or pseudo IV and DV) between which a relationship could have been stated. If there were not two suitable variables, the code 'not applicable' was used.
1. Statement of NO relationship/cause: e.g. 'no difference'; 'persists without'; 'does not result in'; 'no significant extra risk'; 'added no benefit'.

2. Statement of correlation: Meaning remains if the variables in the statement are reversed; e.g. 'associated with'; 'related to'; 'varies with'; 'increases as'; 'decreases as'; 'have higher/lower rates of'; 'linear relationship';

3. Ambiguous statement of correlation/cause: Strictly does not state cause, but contains stronger implication of direct relationship than level 2; e.g. 'linked to'; 'predicts'; 'connected to'; 'more successful'; 'had difficulty';

4. Conditional cause: Causal statement (examples in level 6) preceded by conditional, such as 'might', 'could', 'may', 'appears'; or a statement that implies 'might cause', e.g. 'likely to be a critical event', 'demonstrates potential'.
5. Can cause: Causal statement (examples in level 6) preceded by 'can'. ... Thus we grouped 'could' with 'might' in category 4.

6. Causal statement: Direct causal statement; e.g. 'enhances', 'increases' [as transitive verb - X increases Y], 'decreases', 'cuts', 'ameliorates'; 'influences'; 'prevents'; 'raises/reduces'; 'enables'; 'determines'; 'is vital for'; 'boosts/improves'; 'drives'; 'leads to'; 'transforms'; encourages' etc.
Where statements of different levels were made within the analysed segments of text, stronger statements trumped weaker ones.

Separately, we also coded whether or not the statement of relationship was explicitly probabilistic – for example, 'correlated with the risk of...' (correlational probabilistic); 'raises the chance of...' (causal probabilistic); Further probabilistic words/phrases included: 'likelihood'; 'makes more likely'; 'tendency'; 'rate'.
sources.verify_against: done: ww1 text (pdftotext) lines 72-108, read 2026-10-30. Note the appendix says 'the 6 levels of relationship statement' while listing codes 0-6; the article says 'seven point scale'.

entries.cue: Sumner level-6 verb, present 3rd person, transitive (enhances/increases/decreases/cuts/ameliorates/influences/prevents/raises/reduces/enables/determines/boosts/improves/drives/transforms/encourages)
entries.source_quote: 6. Causal statement: Direct causal statement; e.g. 'enhances', 'increases' [as transitive verb - X increases Y], 'decreases', 'cuts', 'ameliorates'; 'influences'; 'prevents'; 'raises/reduces'; 'enables'; 'determines'; 'is vital for'; 'boosts/improves'; 'drives'; 'leads to'; 'transforms'; encourages' etc. [article: “drinking wine increases cancer risk”]
entries.pattern_note: Transitive use approximated by: no determiner before (the/an/a/no/any increases = noun), and the next word is not a preposition/conjunction/auxiliary ('increases in', 'increases as' (= level 2), 'increases were'). 'raises the question/concern(s)/possibility' excluded (BioScope hedge 'raises the question of'). Other inflections are handled by the modal and past-tense entries.

entries.cue: Sumner level-6 verb after a modal / 'appears to' (may increase, can reduce, appears to improve …)
entries.source_quote: 4. [article: “drinking wine might increase cancer risk”, “drinking wine can increase cancer risk”]
entries.pattern_note: Base-form verb directly after a modal/'appears to'. The span includes the modal; the modal itself then downgrades the cue to 4/5 via `modifiers`. Bare 'to' + verb ('to determine whether', 'to reduce the risk') is NOT matched (purpose clauses in methods/advice).

entries.cue: Sumner level-6 verb, past/-ing forms that are rarely adjectival (prevented, enabled, ameliorated, transformed, encouraged, boosted, influenced/influencing, drove, driven by)
entries.source_quote: 6. entries.pattern_note: Inflections of the quoted verbs. Excluded: hyphenated/‘log transformed’, 'transforming' (transforming growth factor), 'encouraging' (adjective), 'enhanced/improved' (mostly adjectival), 'determined' (methods: 'was determined', 'to determine').

entries.cue: increase / reduce the risk (causal probabilistic: X increases/raises/reduces the risk/chance/rate of Y)
entries.source_quote: 'raises the chance of...' (causal probabilistic) — 6. Causal statement: Direct causal statement; e.g. 'enhances', 'increases' [as transitive verb - X increases Y], 'decreases', 'cuts', 'ameliorates'; 'influences'; 'prevents'; 'raises/reduces'; 'enables'; 'determines'; 'is vital for'; 'boosts/improves'; 'drives'; 'leads to'; 'transforms'; encourages' etc. [article: “drinking wine increases cancer risk”]
entries.pattern_note: Past tense counts as verbal only with a determiner before the risk noun ('increased the risk'); 'increased risk' / 'an increased risk' / 'associated with increased cancer rates' are adjectival = level 2 (article example). v2 used a determiner lookbehind list instead.

entries.cue: increased / reduced + outcome noun (past or base form, X increased/reduced weight)
entries.pattern_note: Object-noun list (levels/symptoms/weight/events/mortality/glucose/pressure) and the preceding-word exclusions (determiners, with/of/and/or/had/has/have/included/including/showed/in/for/by) are PROJECT patterns to separate verb use ('Semaglutide reduced weight') from participial adjectives ('included increased lipase levels'). KNOWN RISK: other adjectival contexts ('patients reported increased symptoms') still score 6 — review.

sentence_rule.description: 1) Run all `entries` patterns (re.IGNORECASE; (?-i:...) groups case-sensitive) on the NFKC view of the sentence (W5 p.29; contractions preserved, W5 p.32 Option 1). Entries whose type is in evidence_flag_types never set the level (evidence_flags only). 2) Per cue, effective level: (a) a level>=2 cue whose span overlaps a level-1 cue ('associated with' inside 'was not associated with') is negated -> 1; (b) else a level>=2 cue that starts within negation_window_tokens tokens AFTER a negation modifier, with no clause boundary (negation_scope_boundary_pattern) in between, is negated -> 1 (review_flag negation_window_applied); (c) else a level-6 cue preceded (anywhere earlier in the sentence, or inside its own span) by may/might/could/appears (or a project level-4 extension) -> 4, else by 'can' -> 5. 3) Sentence level = MAX effective level (Sumner: 'stronger statements trumped weaker ones'). There is NO no-relationship override any more (v2 rule removed). 4) If the sentence has both an effective level-1 cue and an effective level>=2 cue -> review_flag mixed_levels_review (Sumner coded IV–DV pairs by hand; a sentence may hold several). 5) No cue -> 0. 6) collapsed_ko = collapse_map.level_to_collapsed[level]. 7) explicitly_probabilistic per probabilistic_rule (separate binary code). 8) hedges/boosters never change the level; they are counted and listed for the 번역 검수 sheet.
sentence_rule.source: sumner2014_appendix (levels, modifiers, strongest-statement rule, probabilistic code) + vincze2008 (negation keywords; clause boundary markers) + w5_lecture p.29-33 + notion_plan_v2 ⑤

status.highest_claim_rule: verified_source_text — sumner2014_appendix: 'Where statements of different levels were made within the analysed segments of text, stronger statements trumped weaker ones.'; article: 'the presence of stronger statements trumped weaker ones'
status.modifier_position_rule: project_operationalisation — 'preceded by' is implemented as: the modifier starts before the end of the level-6 cue anywhere in the same sentence (no window, no clause check). HEURISTIC.
status.negated_causal_verb_is_level_1: verified_source_text for 'does not result in' (appendix level-1 example); other negated verbs are project_extension_of_verified_category
status.overlap_negation: project_operationalisation — a level>=2 cue inside a level-1 cue span is the same statement, not a second claim
status.negation_window_tokens: project_addition — PROJECT HEURISTIC (Sumner coded whole statements by hand; BioScope resolves negation scope syntactically). Report it and check with human validation.
status.negation_scope_boundary: project_extension_of_verified_category — vincze2008: 'Generally, punctuation marks or conjunctions function as scope boundary markers in the corpus'. The specific boundary list (', ; :' followed by space; but/whereas/although/though/while/however) is a project choice.
status.mixed_levels_review: project_addition — review flag only (does not change the level)
status.sentence_as_unit: project_addition — HEURISTIC: see unit_of_analysis (Sumner coded main-claim IV–DV statements, not sentences)
status.hedge_booster_counts: hyland2005 lists unverified_from_memory, except hedges verified in vincze2008 (see hedges[*].status)
status.evidence_flags_not_levels: project_addition — effect_measure / descriptive_frequency entries are evidence flags, not levels
status.removed_in_v3: no_relationship_precedence (v2: any level-1 cue forced the sentence to 1, overriding the strongest-claim rule; flag no_relationship_overrides_level>=5). Removed because the appendix says stronger statements trump weaker ones.

sentence_rule.negation_window_direction: before the cue (negation precedes the relationship word in English: 'was not associated', 'no increased risk', 'did not increase')
sentence_rule.tokenizer_for_window: W5 lecture p.14 TOKEN_PATTERN = [A-Za-z]+(?:'[A-Za-z]+)+|[A-Za-z]+|\d+(?:\.\d+)? on the NFKC view.

agreement_evaluation.description: For Notion ⑥: compare collapsed_ko of each English source sentence with the Korean-lexicon label of its translation (same sentence_id). Report simple agreement rate and Cohen's kappa; disagreement rows go to the 번역 검수 sheet.
agreement_evaluation.status: project procedure; implemented as preprocess_abstracts.py stage 'agreement' (simple agreement + Cohen's kappa via sklearn.metrics.cohen_kappa_score). The Korean-lexicon label input does not exist yet (no Korean certainty lexicon in the repo); until then the stage reads ko_level_human from review_sheet.csv or --ko-labels JSON and otherwise reports status=deferred.

evidence_flag_types_note: project_addition — Sumner 2014 는 관계 '진술'을 코딩하므로 통계량 이름(HR/OR/RR/IRR/95% CI/P value)이나 빈도 기술(prevalence/incidence of)만으로는 level 을 주지 않는다. 확률 단어(risk/rate/odds/hazard/likelihood)는 Sumner 의 별도 이진 코드 'explicitly probabilistic' 으로 probabilistic_cues 에서 처리한다(v3).

unit_of_analysis.sumner2014: Sumner 등은 사람 코더가 '주장(main claims)' 단위로 IV–DV 쌍과 그 관계 진술을 뽑아 코딩했다. 보도자료·뉴스는 제목+첫 두 문장, 학술논문(JA)은 초록과 논의(abstract and discussion).
sumner2014_quotes: the IV (or pseudo IV in correlational designs), DV and stated relationship between them (if any) were extracted from the main claims, which were operationalized as the title plus first two sentences in PRs and news. For the JA, main claims were defined within the abstract and discussion sections.
For journal articles we used the abstract and discussion. We used a seven point scale to rate increasing levels of determinism, where the presence of stronger statements trumped weaker ones
unit_of_analysis.this_project: PROJECT OPERATIONALISATION (heuristic): 초록의 문장마다 정규식으로 단서를 찾아 같은 척도를 적용한다. IV–DV 쌍을 식별하지 않으며, 한 문장에 여러 IV–DV 진술이 있으면 문장 안에서 '가장 강한 진술' 규칙을 적용한다. level 0 은 Sumner 의 'No relationship stated (but could have been)'와 'not applicable'(두 변수가 없음)을 구분하지 않는다.

probabilistic_cues.pattern_note: up to 3 words between make and more/less likely; 'less' is a project variant

probabilistic_cues.note: Epidemiological probability nouns (odds ratio, hazard ratio, incidence).

probabilistic_rule.description: Sumner 2014 coded, separately from the 0-6 level, 'whether or not the statement of relationship was explicitly probabilistic' (binary). score_sentence() lists matched probabilistic_cues and sets explicitly_probabilistic = (any matched) AND (sentence level >= 1, i.e. a statement of relationship or of no relationship exists). Probabilistic words never change the level.
probabilistic_rule.source_quote: Separately, we also coded whether or not the statement of relationship was explicitly probabilistic – for example, 'correlated with the risk of...' (correlational probabilistic); 'raises the chance of...' (causal probabilistic); Further probabilistic words/phrases included: 'likelihood'; 'makes more likely'; 'tendency'; 'rate'.
probabilistic_rule.gating_status: project_operationalisation — requiring level >= 1 is the project's reading of 'the statement of relationship'; per-sentence regex is a heuristic (see unit_of_analysis).
